q: This study aims to empirically investigate whether instructions documented in agent context files are reflected in agent-generated software artifacts.
r: Include: empirical study of coding agents' adherence to instructions in context files (AGENTS.md-style), group (b).

q: This paper studies whether a short value statement in an agent’s persistent instruction file changes not only how well the agent performs but also what it builds.
r: Include: tests the effect of content of a persistent instruction file on a coding agent's output, group (b); tasks are not application-level but (b) is not narrowed.

q: we introduce Spark, a novel shared agentic memory architecture
r: Include: shared experiential memory mechanism for coding agents, evaluated on code generation quality, group (b) (memory).

q: This paper presents the first large-scale empirical study to characterize this emerging form of developer-provided context.
r: Include: empirical study of 401 repositories' Cursor rules, a context mechanism for AI coding assistants, group (b).

q: We introduce OctoBench to evaluate how models follow heterogeneous instructions in agentic coding tasks.
r: Include: benchmark of coding agents following repository policy files, skills and instructions in agentic coding scaffolds, group (b).

q: We introduces SWE-ContextBench, a benchmark for studying context learning in repository-level coding agents.
r: Include: benchmark on reusing prior experience/memory as context for coding agents with cost and time metrics; group (b) memory, so not narrowed by EC6 despite SWE-bench base.

q: in a complementary end-to-end study using the natural pool across four coding agents
r: IC1: contribution is a retrieval/routing model for selecting skills in an 80K pool; coding agents only appear in a supplementary downstream check.

q: The present experiments measure file-level localization rather than final patch correctness.
r: EC6: benchmark for repository-knowledge systems measures file prediction (code understanding/localization from PR tasks), not code development by an agent.

q: LLM-based coding agents rely on skills
r: Include: empirical study of 55,315 agent skills and token-efficiency optimization with functional quality evaluation, group (b) (skills).

q: effective SE agent skills should be evaluated and evolved for both task success and inference cost
r: Include: multi-objective optimization of agent skills for SE tasks, 10 repetitions per task, pass rate and cost measured, group (b).
